0: Every run starts with a task. In a debate all the debaters get the same question, and each has a side.
1: The first Debater argues for the ban. Debaters speak one at a time, in order, not at the same time.
3: The first argument. It goes into the transcript that the next Debater will read.
4: A handoff records the turn for the Judge, who reads everything at the end.
5: The second Debater argues against. It sees the first argument and answers it.
9: The third Debater is for the ban again. It sees both earlier arguments.
13: The fourth Debater, against. It answers the previous Debater directly.
17: Round 2 begins: the first Debater speaks again, now with the whole of round 1 in front of it.
23: A turn in round 2 builds on what the other side conceded. The debate is moving.
31: The last turn of the last round. The debaters now agree on the conditions and argue about timing.
33: The Judge starts only after all rounds are done. It is a stronger model, because judging needs more care.
35: The verdict: which side argued better and why. It becomes the final answer.
36: The run ends. The final answer is the Judge's verdict.
